p01.why: Each reference needs a temporary character array from a braced literal; Clang and EDG make it and accept, GCC rejects (Q-0166).

p02.why: The braced literal has the referenced type, so the binding is direct to an lvalue, which an rvalue reference cannot take.

p03.why: The list makes a temporary Point, and a non-const lvalue reference cannot bind to it.

p04.why: r binds to a temporary int holding 1, so the later change to l does not reach r and the addresses differ.

p05.why: A reference member of an aggregate initialized with braces extends the temporary Note, so it is not destroyed before the read.

p06.why: a binds directly to x, and b binds to a temporary holding 2.

p07.why: Two values cannot initialize a temporary int.

p08.why: The lvalue long converts to a temporary int that r binds to, and the temporary keeps the value 1.

p09.why: A braced function name binds a function reference as after =, and an rvalue reference to a function type binds to a function.

p10.why: Clang and EDG bind the braced array directly to the reference of unknown bound; GCC makes a one-element temporary and rejects (Q-0164).

p11.why: EDG rejects a noexcept function in braces; the other compilers bind as after = (Q-0165).

p12.why: Each braced element has the referenced type, so each reference binds directly, and moved binds to an xvalue of its own type.

p13.why: The braced list makes a temporary int, and 2.5 to int is narrowing.

p14.why: Three values do not fit a temporary array of two elements.

p15.why: An rvalue reference must not bind to an lvalue of a derived class.

p16.why: An rvalue reference to a function type binds to a function.

p17.why: GCC rejects an overloaded function name in braces; the others pick show(int) as after = (Q-0165).

p18.why: An rvalue reference must not bind to an lvalue of its own type.

p19.why: Binding through a reference member does not extend the Holder, so it ends at the semicolon, and x refers to target, which still holds 5.

p20.why: The braced element binds directly as after =, and a non-const reference cannot drop the const of the array elements.

p21.why: The temporary needs the explicit constructor; GCC and EDG reject, Clang accepts (Q-0150).

p22.why: Clang warns about a temporary bound to a reference member of an object from new, so -Werror rejects it; GCC does not warn and compiles.

p23.why: A non-const reference cannot bind to a const int.

p24.why: Binding to a member of the temporary extends the whole Pair, so the '|' is logged before any destructor runs.

p25.why: A base reference binds directly to the derived object and sees v = 7.

p26.why: Each braced element has the referenced type or a derived class, so each reference binds directly to the constexpr global.

p27.why: Binding through a null pointer is undefined; GCC and Clang 22 reject it in constant evaluation, EDG 7.0 and Clang 18 accept (Q-0110).

p28.why: A static_cast to a reference type extends the temporary, so 2 is recorded before the destructor's 1.

p29.why: A volatile lvalue reference must not bind to an rvalue.

p30.why: Every reference binds directly to an lvalue of its type or a function.

p31.why: The extended temporary is destroyed with its block when the exception leaves it, so ended is 1 in the handler.

p32.why: The returned reference outlives x, and reading it during constant evaluation is rejected.

p33.why: The temporary ends at the end of the full expression, so kept dangles; I guess AddressSanitizer reports the use after scope, but the spec does not say whether it does.

p34.why: Empty braces would give an array of zero elements; Clang and EDG reject, GCC accepts (Q-0149).

p35.why: A reference member of an aggregate initialized with parentheses does not extend the temporary, so reading h.n in constant evaluation is rejected.

p36.why: In parentheses the initializer of a reference must hold exactly one expression.

p37.why: GCC accepts a parenthesized list of several values for an aggregate reference; Clang and EDG reject (Q-0151).

p38.why: Each braced list makes an extended temporary: Point {1,2}, Point {3,0}, and a Box that ends at its block.

p39.why: A reference member of an object from new does not extend the temporary, so each Note ends at its full expression and trace is 1234.

p40.why: An xvalue of the same type binds the const reference directly to g, so r sees 5.

p41.why: Each list makes an extended temporary array, with missing elements zero, and the rvalue reference can change its array.

p42.why: The list makes a temporary array of three elements that the reference can read and change, whatever bound each compiler records.

p43.why: The sequence to int& forms in spite of the bit-field, wins as an identity over int to long, and the chosen call is then rejected.

p44.why: Each reference adds qualifiers or drops the bound and binds directly to cells.

p45.why: Clang and EDG make a temporary int and reject the non-const binding; GCC binds through the conversion function and accepts (Q-0157).

p46.why: EDG 7.0 rejects binding to an element of an array member of a temporary; Clang and GCC extend the temporary and the run returns 0 (Q-0109).

p47.why: Parentheses, the selected operand of ?:, and the right operand of a comma all extend the temporaries, which end with the block.

p48.why: The temporary lives as long as the global reference.

p49.why: A non-const lvalue reference must not bind to a bit-field.

p50.why: a and b bind to temporaries, and c binds to x through the xvalue cast.

p51.why: The rvalue reference must not drop const from the object.

p52.why: Clang and EDG make temporaries holding 1 and the run returns 0; GCC binds through the conversion function to target, so it gives a different result or rejects the rvalue binding (Q-0157).

p53.why: Both const references bind to temporaries holding 5 and 7.

p54.why: A const reference to a bit-field binds to a temporary copy, so the later change does not reach r.

p55.why: The extended temporaries end at the block in reverse order, b then a, and the unbound temporary t ends at its statement.

p56.why: A non-const reference to int cannot bind to a long.

p57.why: The braced array has the referenced type, so the binding is direct to an lvalue, which an rvalue reference cannot take.

p58.why: A reference to an array of unknown bound binds to an array of known bound.

p59.why: The reference binds to the member returned by the conversion function, which does not extend the Cell, so 1 is marked before 2 and r is never read.

p60.why: Each const reference binds directly to its lvalue, so it shares the address and sees later changes.

p61.why: A returned reference does not extend the temporary, so r dangles and the read in constant evaluation is rejected.

p62.why: GCC and EDG keep the declared type int(&&)[]; Clang gives the reference the bound 3, so the static_assert fails there (Q-0149).
